title: Room assembled from one wall module + window panes (POV CSG)
description: `#declare wall = box{<0,0,0><10,10,0.2>}` is declared once and instanced four times by rotation; window_pane is a second module punched through. The room is a *composition of modules*, which is exactly the feature ordering Atta's architecture family needs.

parameters.name: wall_width
parameters.description: wall module width (x of the box)

parameters.name: wall_height
parameters.description: wall module height (y of the box)

parameters.name: wall_thickness
parameters.description: wall thickness; drives the window reveal depth

constraints.why: a pane wider than its wall leaves the room open; the cut must stay strictly inside the wall face
thinner walls print with no window reveal, so the opening reads as a decal rather than a hole

nomination.reason: a room as N wall modules + N openings is parametrisable in a way a single mesh shell is not; Atta has no architecture family at all yet

title: Room shell as one hollow box with a tiled surface normal
description: room_exterior = box{<-0.2,-0.2,0.2><5.2,5.2,-5.2>}: a single shell that is then given a gradient tile normal. Cheap, watertight, and the opposite trade-off from the wall-module room: one closed solid, no per-wall parts.

parameters.name: shell_overshoot
parameters.description: wall offset outside the nominal box

parameters.name: tile_pitch
parameters.description: gradient x factor of the tile normal

constraints.why: the overshoot is subtracted from the interior; beyond half the smallest extent the interior vanishes

title: Door opening as a shallow cut in a 1-unit wall (POV box room)
description: The room is six boxes; the door is box{<7.5,0,-10><9.0,4,-9.9>} — a 1.5 x 4 opening cut only 0.1 deep into a 1.0 wall. A minimal, readable statement of the opening rule: opening depth must not exceed wall thickness.

parameters.name: room_size
parameters.description: interior extent of the box room

constraints.why: a cut deeper than the wall punches through and the opening becomes a window at a different height

title: Quadtree facade subdivision grammar (4 children + 4 rotated leaves)
description: SHAPE2 emits four SHAPE3 leaves at r90/r180/r-90, then recurses into four children at (+-.75, +-.75) scaled 0.5 and flipped — the canonical quadtree panelling rule. Each level halves the panel and doubles the count.

parameters.name: subdivision_scale
parameters.description: child scale (s .5 on every recursive successor)

parameters.name: child_offset
parameters.description: child translation in units of the parent (x/y +-.75)

parameters.name: leaf_rotation
parameters.description: rotation applied to each of the four leaves (r 90)

constraints.why: a child scale >= 1 makes the recursion diverge — panels grow and overlap instead of tiling
children offset further than 1 unit leave the parent cell, which turns panelling into scattered ornament
4^depth panels: depth 8 is 65536 faces from one rule

nomination.reason: recursive panel subdivision is how facade/wall families get real variety from one rule; Atta's Spec v3 has no recursion

title: Vertical growth grammar: stack with scale decay + stochastic branches
description: SHAPE2 stacks itself with y+=1 and s=0.999, and with small probabilities branches to a 10x5 slab or resets. That is a tower/mast law: a monotone stack, a slow taper, and rare lateral features.

parameters.name: feature_probability
parameters.description: weight of the rare slab rule (rule 0.0005)

parameters.name: levels
parameters.description: stack height in steps; total height = levels*stack_step

constraints.why: a per-level scale above 1 makes the stack widen without bound
the growth law has no stopping rule of its own; levels is the only cap on height

title: Dihedral-6 ornament: recursive square bars under CF::Dihedral, 6
description: CF::Symmetry = CF::Dihedral, 6 mirrors the whole composition 6-fold, while SHAPE3 lays out bars in x with alternating ±1.5 deg rotations. One rule set, 12-fold visual richness — the cheapest ornament generator in the set.

parameters.name: symmetry_order
parameters.description: n of CF::Dihedral, n (reflective symmetry order)

constraints.why: dihedral order must be an integer; a fractional n has no rotation group to close
bar tilts above ~10 deg break the mirror seam and the ornament stops reading as symmetric

title: Odd-order dihedral rosette (CF::Dihedral, 13)
description: The same production system at dihedral order 13 — an odd order has no mirror-pair degeneracy, so the rosette has a single seam. Useful as the boundary case against the even-order ornament.

parameters.name: shape_count
parameters.description: distinct shape declarations in the grammar

constraints.why: this record documents the odd-order case; even orders close differently (see cfdg_dihedral_ornament6)

title: Spiral ornament by rotate+scale decay with dihedral mirror pairs
description: SHAPE3 recurses with r 355.25 (i.e. -4.75 deg), x 10, s 0.99 — a decaying spiral. Two copies at flip 90 give the reflection pair, and CF::Dihedral 6 closes it into a medallion.

parameters.name: mirror_flip
parameters.description: flip angle of the paired copy (flip 90)

constraints.why: a spiral with scale >= 1 grows outward and consumes the canvas
total rotation beyond ~8 turns aliases into concentric rings

title: 40x20 panel grid with per-cell stochastic transforms (facade generator)
description: A doubly nested loop (40 columns x 20 rows, unit cells) picks a random number and applies one of three branches per cell: scaled/rotated/jittered square, or alternatives; hue varies as sin(2*pi*rand(10)*i*j/400). This is the cheapest credible facade-panel distribution law.

parameters.name: branch_split
parameters.description: if (rnd<33) / (33..66) / else — the three-way branch threshold

constraints.why: panels scaled or jittered beyond the cell pitch overlap their neighbours and the grid reads as noise
the three branches are a partition of [0,100); a threshold outside that range collapses one branch to probability 0

nomination.reason: a facade family needs a *distribution* over panels, not a single panel; three-way stochastic branching over a grid is the minimum viable version and it is 8 parameters

title: pyramid_z(a, b, zmin, height) — tapered roof prism with an explicit base rectangle
description: A pyramid frustum defined by its base rectangle, base height and total height. The only roof primitive in the corpus that exposes both the base aspect and the rise as independent parameters.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: rise from zmin to the apex plane

constraints.why: a zero rise is a flat plate, not a roof

title: half_space(norm, point) — the plane primitive that makes walls cheap
description: A half-space is the primitive architecture actually needs: cut a solid by a plane to get a wall, a floor or a sloped roof face. norm plus a point is two parameters and no boolean history.

parameters.name: norm
parameters.description: plane normal (vec3); sign selects which side is solid

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: distance to shift the plane along the normal

constraints.why: a zero normal makes the field constant — the half-space becomes all space or no space
an unnormalised normal scales every distance in the tree, which silently breaks blending and shell offsets

title: Tower growth, forked variant: paired ±45° branches at 5% probability
description: Same stacking law as the base tower (y+=1, s=0.999) but the branch rule emits a *mirrored pair* at flip -45/+45 with s=0.8, plus a r=90 rotation branch and a rare 10x5 feature at weight 0.0005. Distinguishes 'fork' from 'taper' as a growth mode.

parameters.name: twist_probability
parameters.description: weight of the r=90 branch (second rule 0.05)

parameters.name: anchor_offset
parameters.description: x offset of the whole grammar (x 9)

constraints.why: the two branch rules use +45 and -45; equal magnitudes are what keep the fork symmetric about the trunk
rule weights compete; a sum above 1 leaves no weight for the trunk and the tower never grows

title: Tower growth, nested-filament variant: trunk of stacked squares with sub-branches
description: Third variant: the trunk rule is the same (y+=1, s=0.999) but the leaf is a nested square filament (SHAPE6: y+=0.98, s=0.98, self-recursive) that can hand off to a second filament with r=0.1 or r=0.51. Two competing filament laws, chosen by weight.

parameters.name: switch_probability
parameters.description: weight of the handoff to the second filament (rule 0.005)

parameters.name: slow_twist
parameters.description: rotation per filament step of filament 2 (r 0.1)

parameters.name: handoff_twist
parameters.description: rotation at the handoff back to filament 1 (r 0.51)

constraints.why: the filament must shrink at least as fast as the trunk or it grows out of the silhouette
at zero the second filament law is unreachable and the variant degenerates to the base tower

title: Context Free — interrupted tradition (metadata only)
description: The reference CFDG implementation: weighted rule selection, per-successor transform modifiers, global CF::Symmetry groups, and a tiling mode (CF::Tile). Documents the semantics that the MIT example corpus depends on.

nomination.reason: defines the exact rule-weighting and symmetry semantics an Atta grammar op must reproduce

notes: Tier C / GPL lineage: metadata-only by policy. Licence evidence: LICENSE.txt. No code may be taken; the value is the idea (see work/harvest/deep/NOTE.md §4).
